overview.problem: Design-first frontend overhaul of 3 Eamos surfaces (Landing /, Variant Evidence Report /report, Workbench /workbench) to a 'scientific accuracy meets quiet luxury' feel, driven by 4 ingested design-philosophy docs. Deliverable: per-page reviewable step-by-step task plans. Frontend-only; evolve DESIGN.md v2 tokens (add navy-header tier); navy = header/chrome ONLY; net-new surfaces = working visual shells on sample data; plan approved by user BEFORE implementation.
overview.approach: Approach B: build shared primitives once (navy-header chrome tier tokens + one shared scroll-transition SearchShell), then 3 independently-reviewable per-page milestone tracks (Landing / Report / Workbench). Net-new (multi-variant/VCF, ancestry heatmap, export menu) = sample-data visual shells, no backend.ts reshape. Evolve DESIGN.md v2, not rewrite. Verification = npm run build clean + vitest 73/73 + contract canary 40/40 (no backend.ts shape change) + browser-verify Workbench.

decisions.decision: Approach B: build shared primitives once (navy-header chrome tier tokens + extended SearchShell), then 3 independently-reviewable per-page tracks (Landing/Report/Workbench).
decisions.reasoning: 4 docs demand a structural+mood delta not just a retheme -> minimal-retheme (A) under-delivers and big-bang (C) is not independently reviewable nor bisectable against vitest 73/73 + contract 40/40 -> a foundation milestone plus 3 parallel page tracks is the only option that satisfies the per-page-reviewable SHOULD while bounding regression blast radius.

decisions.decision: Landing-only scroll-transition search: shared SearchShell gains an optional scroll-shrink/sticky behavior gated to the landing surface; Report and Workbench keep todays static compact in-nav search.
decisions.reasoning: User ruled ScrollSrch=Landing-only -> a global scroll-transition would fight the dense evidence-table reading mode on /report and the fixed 3-col canvas on /workbench -> gate the behavior behind an explicit landing-only prop plus prefers-reduced-motion guard so one component still serves all three headers without imposing motion where it harms legibility.

decisions.decision: Workbench retires its bespoke .nav-wrap header and adopts the shared navy TopNav + ModePill; the 3-col shell (64px rail / 1fr canvas / 360px side panel) is re-pixel-verified in a browser under the new shared header height.
decisions.reasoning: User ruled WbNav=Adopt shared TopNav -> two divergent chromes double maintenance and break cross-surface continuity -> consolidate on the navy TopNav, but a different header height shifts the canvas viewport math so an explicit browser/pixel re-verification of the 3-col shell is mandatory before the Workbench track is done.

decisions.decision: Multi-variant realized as a slim VARIANT TAB STRIP top-most-left, directly beneath the sticky navy header and ABOVE the Variant Hero Summary, on its own axis, with an Import VCF affordance beside it, all sample/placeholder driven. A Table-view comparison grid is RESERVED in layout but NOT built this pass.
decisions.reasoning: User ruled MultiVar=light shell as a top-left tab strip -> browser/editor-style tabs are elegant for ~2-6 variants but the doc cautions large tab sets do not scale -> ship only the tab strip + Import VCF affordance on sample data now, keep it on its own axis so it never competes with header or in-page section nav, and reserve (but do not build) the Table view as the documented large-VCF escape hatch for a later cycle.

decisions.decision: Net-new feature surfaces (variant tab strip + Import VCF, ancestry heatmap, export menu) are working visual shells on sample/placeholder data with NO backend.ts contract shape change.
decisions.reasoning: User explicitly chose (Tier-1, recorded in invisible_knowledge.tradeoffs: visual shells now, real data via Codex later, to reduce repetitive FE<->BE back-and-forth) -> this user decision is the primary backing, reinforced by Hard Rule 5 (contract changes are backend-led, test_frontend_contract.py canary is 40/40) so reshaping backend.ts here would break the canary and cross the FE/BE lane -> shells consume FE-only additive sample types from src/lib so Codex can wire real data later without a FE redesign.

decisions.decision: Evolve DESIGN.md v2 by adding an additive navy-header chrome tier (navy = header/chrome ONLY, NOT page background; white/off-white content surfaces; teal accents; neutral grays + subtle warm neutral) rather than rewriting the design system.
decisions.reasoning: User clarified explicitly (Tier-1, recorded in context.constraints and RA-003): navy = header/chrome ONLY, not page background, white/off-white content, teal buttons/accents, neutral+warm-neutral -> this user ruling, not just the technical legibility inference, is the primary backing; a v3 navy-dominant rewrite would also contradict the preserved clinical core (0.5px hairlines, semantic classification colours, no weight>700, motion only via tokens) and risk dense-table legibility -> therefore add a scoped header/chrome token tier, reuse the existing focus glow + elevation/motion tokens, and change nothing in the content palette.

decisions.decision: ACCEPTED-RISK / VALIDATED: the design docs Gene/Sequence Viewer Page is treated as the existing /workbench surface. Validated against the codebase before planning.
decisions.reasoning: Assumption was silently load-bearing: if wrong, the redesign retargets the wrong surface -> validated against the codebase: App.tsx routes only `/report`->ReportPage and `/workbench`->WorkbenchPage (no separate Gene/Sequence Viewer route), and README.md (lines 10/190/194) defines Workbench (/workbench) as the sequence-viewer surface -> mapping confirmed, no residual risk; logged here so the assumption is no longer silent.

decisions.decision: ACCEPTED-RISK: sample data is treated as sufficient for all shells; existing sample modules cover report/workbench, and the three net-new shells get NEW FE-only additive sample modules created within this plan.
decisions.reasoning: Assumption sample-data-sufficient-for-all-shells was unvalidated and load-bearing -> codebase check: src/lib/sample-report.ts + src/lib/workbench/*-sample.ts (gene-viewer-sample, primer-sample, crispr-sample, sample-rpe65-v2, etc.) already cover existing report/workbench surfaces; the three net-new shells (variant tab strip, ancestry heatmap, export menu) have NO existing sample file -> M-003 explicitly CREATES sample-variants.ts and sample-ancestry.ts as additive FE-only modules (CI-M-003-001/002) and ExportMenu is no-op needing no data -> residual risk reduced to schema-shape-only, accepted because shells are FE-only and Codex wires real shapes later (DL-005).

+## Navy Chrome Tier
+
+A distinct header/chrome surface layer. Navy applies **only** to the top navigation
+bar -- never to page backgrounds or content surfaces.
+
+### Token additions (additive -- extend `:root` in `src/index.css`)
+
+```css
+--chrome-h:          56px;             /* shared nav height token */
+--chrome-bg:         #0f2744;          /* nav bar fill -- navy */
+--chrome-bg-hover:   #162f52;          /* subtle lighten on interactive chrome items */
+--chrome-border:     rgba(255,255,255,0.08); /* hairline on navy bg */
+--chrome-ink:        #e8edf3;          /* primary text on navy */
+--chrome-ink-2:      rgba(232,237,243,0.65); /* secondary / label text on navy */
+--chrome-ink-4:      rgba(232,237,243,0.40); /* hint / placeholder on navy */
+--chrome-teal:       #22c491;          /* teal brightened +15% L for navy bg contrast */
+```
+
+### Design rules
+
+- `--chrome-bg` is the exact background of every navy header. Nothing else uses it.
+- White/off-white surfaces (`--bg`, `--bg-soft`) remain for all content below the nav.
+- Teal buttons and accents on chrome surfaces use `--chrome-teal` (not `--teal`) to
+  meet 4.5:1 contrast on the dark background.
+- The `0.5px solid var(--chrome-border)` hairline replaces `var(--line)` on chrome.
+- `ModePill` on the navy chrome: inactive items use `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)` pill bg;
+  active item uses `--ink-2` fill + white text; inactive text uses `--chrome-ink-2`.
+- SearchShell input on navy chrome: pill bg `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)`, border
+  `var(--chrome-border)`, placeholder text `var(--chrome-ink-4)`, text
+  `var(--chrome-ink)`. Focus glow uses the existing teal ring.
+
+### Usage
+
+```html
+<!-- TopNav with navy chrome tone -->
+<TopNav tone="navy" />
+```
+
+```css
+.top-nav--navy { background: var(--chrome-bg); border-bottom: 0.5px solid var(--chrome-border); }
+.top-nav--navy .nav-search-shell { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); border-color: var(--chrome-border); }
+```
+
 ### Sequence palette (Workbench only)

milestones.name: Report track - variant tab strip + Import VCF shell, content-as-hero rhythm, progressive disclosure, ancestry heatmap + export menu shells
requirements: New FE-only sample-variants.ts and sample-ancestry.ts created with no backend.ts import; VariantTabStrip rendered on its own axis beneath the sticky navy header and above the Variant Hero Summary with an Import VCF affordance and a reserved-but-unbuilt Table-view slot; AncestryHeatmap and ExportMenu shells render on sample data with no real generation; all clinical modules and their order preserved; Report keeps the STATIC compact in-nav search (no scrollTransition)
acceptance_criteria: npm run build clean and vitest 73/73 and contract 40/40 unchanged with no backend.ts shape change; tab strip switches active sample variant and never visually competes with header or section nav; Table view is not rendered this pass; EvidenceTable and InSilicoGrid remain dense and legible with semantic classification colours unchanged; AlphaMissense remains display-off; ExportMenu and Import VCF are visually complete but no-op
tests: npm run build; npm run test; pytest test_frontend_contract.py; browser pixel-verify report tab strip + heatmap + export shells

code_intents.behavior: CREATE a NEW FE-only sample module exporting ~3-5 placeholder variant tab entries (id, gene, hgvs label, classification) plus an active-variant selector default. No backend.ts import or contract reshape; this is illustrative data the tab strip shell binds to so Codex can wire real multi-variant data later.

CREATE a NEW FE-only sample module exporting a small placeholder population-by-region matrix for the ancestry heatmap shell (region labels, cohort labels, frequency cells). No backend.ts contract change; illustrative only.

CREATE a NEW slim VARIANT TAB STRIP component: browser/editor-style tabs for ~2-6 variants from sample-variants.ts, positioned by ReportPage directly beneath the sticky navy header and ABOVE the Variant Hero Summary, on its own axis (visually distinct from in-page section nav, never competes with the header). Includes an Import VCF affordance button beside the tabs (opens a no-op/sample placeholder this pass; no real VCF parsing). Leave horizontal layout room for a future Table view toggle but DO NOT render or build it. Selecting a tab swaps the active sample variant. Tokens existing; teal accent for active tab; 0.5px hairlines.

CREATE a NEW ancestry heatmap visual shell bound to sample-ancestry.ts: a calm matrix of muted-intensity cells with region/cohort labels, legend, 0.5px hairlines, no semantic-classification colours reused, no decorative gradients beyond the <=4% functional wash rule. Sample data only; data-source stamp text indicating placeholder.

CREATE a NEW export menu shell: a quiet dropdown listing PDF / Excel / Citation options that are visually complete but no-op this pass (no real generation). Reuse focus glow ring, chrome/teal accents, motion via tokens with prefers-reduced-motion guard.

COMPOSE the new structure: navy TopNav (tone=navy) with the existing STATIC compact in-nav SearchShell (NO scrollTransition - that is landing-only); then render VariantTabStrip on its own axis directly beneath the sticky header and ABOVE the Variant Hero Summary; keep the 920px content column and numbered modular cards vertical; mount ExportMenu in the report chrome and AncestryHeatmap as a new card/section. Preserve all clinical modules and their order; only add the new shells and apply the content-as-hero rhythm.

Refine VariantHeader to read as the content-as-hero Variant Summary directly below the tab strip: tighten hierarchy and whitespace, keep classification badge semantics and colours unchanged. Replace its window.print() Export PDF tool link reference by deferring export to the new ExportMenu (remove only the now-duplicated trigger; do not alter clinical content).

Keep the existing progressive-disclosure fold as the disclosure exemplar; align its teaser/expand affordance visuals to the refreshed rhythm and ensure motion uses --dur-*/--ease-* with prefers-reduced-motion guard. Classification/criteria logic unchanged.
Apply the quiet-luxury rhythm (spacing, hairlines, restrained type) to LocusContext; no data or contract change.
Restyle InSilicoGrid for dense-but-scannable calm: even cell rhythm, 0.5px hairlines, preserve all predictor semantics and colours. AlphaMissense remains display-OFF as-is; do not re-enable.
Restyle EvidenceTable preserving dense legibility (this is the legibility-critical surface): keep hairlines, muted palette, no navy background; only spacing/type refinements. No column/data change.
Apply rhythm refinements to DiseaseSection; content/contract unchanged.
Apply rhythm refinements to AssociatedConditions; content/contract unchanged.

Align AIStack to the refreshed report rhythm and the navy chrome accents where it sits in chrome; preserve AI evidence-summary behavior and content. Motion via tokens with prefers-reduced-motion guard.
